key_headlines.title: Bank of Korea to Decide on Rate Hike on November 26; Next Year's Growth Forecast Expected to Rise Significantly
key_headlines.summary: The Bank of Korea's monetary policy committee will meet on November 26 to decide whether to raise the base rate by 0.25 percentage points amid persistent inflation and strong economic growth. Market experts unanimously predict a rate increase, with next year's growth forecast expected to rise substantially from the current 2.9% projection.

key_headlines.title: KOSPI Falls 4% on AI Uncertainty; Market Sentiment Severely Dampened
key_headlines.summary: The KOSPI index plummeted 4% and breached the 4,600 level following the weekend collapse of AI-related stocks in the US, with semiconductor stocks declining sharply in tandem. The government indicated readiness for market stabilization measures including potential deployment of market stabilization funds depending on market conditions.

key_headlines.title: South Korea's November Exports Reach Record Pace; Semiconductor Exports Surge Fourfold
key_headlines.summary: South Korea's exports from November 1-20 totaled $77.4 billion, up 101.5% year-over-year with semiconductors accounting for 49.7% of total exports. The trade surplus reached $27.1 billion, the highest for the same period on record, with daily average exports up 95.2%.

key_headlines.title: Semiconductor Boom Expected to Continue into Next Year, 2026 Growth Rate Could Reach 4%
key_headlines.summary: Deputy Prime Minister Lee Hyung-il announced that global semiconductor demand is expected to remain robust through next year and that this year's growth rate could arithmetically reach 4%. He emphasized that the semiconductor industry's strong momentum should continue into 2027.

key_headlines.title: China's Electric Vehicle Imports Surge; South Korea's Trade Deficit with China Hits Record $6 Trillion Won
key_headlines.summary: South Korea's automobile trade deficit with China reached a record high of $6 trillion won in the first 10 months of 2026, driven by surging imports of Tesla electric vehicles produced in Shanghai. South Korea's auto exports to China fell 34.9% while imports surged 79.2% compared to the same period last year.

sections.Hot Economy News: South Korea's economy is facing mixed signals with strong semiconductor-driven export growth contrasting sharply with deteriorating financial market conditions. The KOSPI index collapsed 4% following global AI stock sell-offs, wiping out previous gains and triggering government consideration of emergency market stabilization measures. Despite the market turmoil, exports surged significantly with November 1-20 shipments up 101.5%, semiconductor exports accounting for nearly half of total exports. The government is closely monitoring inflation pressures and economic growth rates ahead of the Bank of Korea's crucial rate decision on November 26, which is expected to result in a 0.25 percentage point rate increase.
sections.Macro & Fiscal Policy: The Bank of Korea will hold its final monetary policy committee meeting of the year on November 26, with market consensus strongly favoring a 0.25 percentage point rate increase to 3.25%. Third-quarter GDP growth exceeded expectations at 1.0%, significantly outperforming the central bank's 0.3% forecast, while core inflation remains elevated in the late 2% range. The IMF has warned that additional tightening measures may be necessary to combat persistent inflation pressures. Next year's growth forecast is expected to be revised upward substantially, potentially above the current 2.9% projection, with the monetary policy committee's interest rate guidance (K dot plot) for six months ahead expected to settle around 3.50%.
sections.Financial Markets: Financial markets experienced severe turbulence as the KOSPI fell 4% and briefly breached the 4,600 level following the weekend collapse of AI-related stocks in the United States. The won-dollar exchange rate approached 1,600 won, raising concerns about currency volatility. Despite efforts to deploy market stabilization funds (not used in 18 years), investor confidence remained severely dampened as foreign investors liquidated positions. Market analysts attribute the volatility to multiple factors including oil price fluctuations, interest rate changes, exchange rate movements, and conflicting investment patterns among different investor types. The government signaled readiness to deploy market stabilization measures while monitoring market conditions and assessing appropriate timing and scale.
sections.Industry & Technology: South Korea's semiconductor sector continues to boom despite broader market uncertainties, with exports surging 101.5% in early November and semiconductor products representing nearly 50% of total exports. However, the automotive industry faces significant headwinds as Chinese electric vehicles, particularly Tesla models manufactured in Shanghai, have rapidly penetrated the Korean market, creating a record $6 trillion won trade deficit with China in just 10 months. The electric vehicle sector has emerged as a critical concern, with the government identifying 2027-2029 as a golden window for market transformation and considering whether to include domestically-produced electric vehicles in production tax credit programs. Deputy Prime Minister Lee indicated that China's semiconductor and electric vehicle sectors are showing robust growth across the board, with Chinese export increases roughly double those of South Korea.
sections.Real Estate: South Korea's housing market shows mixed activity with 15 properties nationwide offering 6,295 units for lease application during the final week of November, representing a 3.7-fold increase compared to the previous week. High-profile lottery apartment offerings have emerged, including a 2 billion won unit in Jamsil and new supplies in Yeongdeungpo and Jongno districts of Seoul. However, the government's plan to increase monthly rent tax deduction limits from 10 million to 12 million won annually is expected to have limited effectiveness, as 94% of tenant households in Seoul fall within the current deduction limit. Daegu city has eased sunshine access requirements for redevelopment and reconstruction projects to facilitate housing supply expansion.
sections.International Economy: Global financial markets have experienced significant instability following AI stock sell-offs, with the US Federal Reserve expected to raise interest rates by 0.25 percentage points at its December meeting, with market attention focused on whether further increases will follow. President Trump blamed the Democratic Party for recent stock market declines, claiming $6 trillion in market capitalization has evaporated since Democratic election victories. Treasury Secretary Bessent publicly warned the Federal Reserve against excessive tightening, arguing that financial conditions have become considerably restrictive despite the government's preference for lower interest rates. Market observers remain concerned about additional rate hikes and their potential impact on global financial conditions and economic growth.
sections.AI & Economy: Wall Street is experiencing growing skepticism about AI investments amid concerns that Democratic control of Congress could expand regulations on AI data centers and intensify export restrictions on China, potentially causing the 'techno-dollar' system to collapse. AI stock sell-offs have triggered surge in volatility indexes as investors reassess the sustainability of massive AI infrastructure investment. Industry leaders warn that AI investment is absorbing semiconductors, electricity, talent, and capital resources at an accelerating pace, potentially crowding out other industries and creating dependency risks for the US economy. Major financial firms are launching AI-focused investment strategies, with Korean investment management companies introducing new target-date funds combining AI industry growth with long-term pension asset management. Industry analysis suggests AI innovation remains crucial for gaming and other sectors facing low growth, though market turbulence is highlighting risks of over-concentration in AI-related assets.
sections.Others: LS Securities has launched an AI-powered investment advisory service called 'LS Connector' in beta, allowing customers to execute various investment functions through natural conversation with AI without opening separate trading platforms. Daewoo Electronics has established Korea's first AI-automated design system for distribution transformers, reducing design lead time by up to 90% by leveraging 80 years of accumulated design data. VUNO, a medical AI company, has launched its fundus image reading AI solution in Brazil after obtaining regulatory approval, beginning its full entry into Latin American markets through an exclusive distribution partnership. Deputy Prime Minister Lee emphasized that youth employment is crucial for addressing economic polarization and indicated the government is pushing to develop the service sector. Intelligence reports suggest Chinese intelligence agencies maintained sustained contact with figures involved in a recent corporate scandal involving Nvidia's former CEO.
